objectives.description: Write and confirm post-write verification passes
objectives.note: CRITICAL FINDING AND FIX mid-objective -- see deviations. First --write attempt correctly refused/rolled back on a stale same-day backup (baier's part07/part08 were already legitimately repaired earlier today by the preceding sweep task, so the day-start backup predated that edit). The rollback ITSELF used the stale backup as its restore target, which is unsafe -- it reverted part07/part08 to their pre-earlier-repair state. No data lost (engine is deterministic; re-running --write against the current code reproduced the earlier repairs plus the new fix in one pass, 86 occurrences, 0 rolled back, verified idempotent). Fixed the underlying rollback-target logic in literature-repair-combining.sh to always use the invocation's own captured pre-edit read, never the on-disk day-level backup, for both the delta baseline and the restore target. Verified via a new scratch multi-session regression fixture proving a rollback under corruption-injection preserves an earlier same-day legitimate edit rather than reverting past it. Corpus-wide dry-run after the fix confirms 0 proposed rewrites across all 60 PDF+markdown directories (full residual ledger regenerated: 819 -> 806 repairable, exactly the 13 almost-equal-to entries cleared, zero drift elsewhere).

deviations.description: Phase 1's post-write rollback target was the on-disk day-start backup.
deviations.reason: Real-corpus write on baier_katoen_2008 exposed that the day-start backup can predate a legitimate earlier-same-day edit (task 403's own repairs to part07/part08 earlier today), making it unsafe as a rollback target -- a coincidental delta mismatch caught it this time, but the design was not principled. Fixed to always restore to the invocation's own captured pre-edit read. Corpus damage was transient (this invocation's own accidental over-rollback) and fully self-healed by re-running the deterministic engine with the corrected code; no external data loss occurred and no other directory was affected (only baier_katoen_2008's part07/part08 were ever in this invocation's write set).
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered — rollback-target logic corrected mid-phase after a real near-miss; see Phase 2's Deviations note in the plan for the full incident writeup)*
